clue.text: Moved into a house but was disillusioned

definitions.meaning: someone who quit their apartment for a house has abandoned the apartment
to be left feeling deflated and let down after hopes fade

explanation.surface: A homeowner moves in, only to find the new place a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting an apartment for a house, and being left deflated, are the two readings of the phrase.

clue.text: Detonated a bomb but acquitted

definitions.meaning: exploded a device, set it going
released without punishment by a court

explanation.surface: A bomber blew something up yet walked free from court.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both exploding a device and excusing someone from a penalty.

clue.text: Spanish celebration feast served up about one

indicators.note: the reworked word goes around the letter for one
food served up is dished out and arranged, so the letters of feast are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A Spanish party where a banquet is dished up for a single guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' rearranges FEAST to FESTA, and 'about' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a Spanish festival or holiday, a public celebration.

clue.text: Tried fencing but was thwarted

definitions.meaning: used the light sword of the fencing sport
was frustrated, had plans blocked

explanation.surface: Someone took up swordplay but got beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A foil is a fencing sword, and to foil also means to frustrate a plan.

clue.text: Perplexed by a description of an anagram

definitions.meaning: confused, bewildered
an anagram has its letters jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: A solver is baffled by how a word puzzle is explained.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means confused, and also literally describes letters scrambled in a rearrangement.

clue.text: Conclude that there is a gale blowing

definitions.meaning: bring to an end, finish off

definitions.text: that there is a gale blowing
definitions.meaning: a strong breeze has risen, taken literally

explanation.surface: Someone decides the weather report says a storm is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish proceedings is a phrasal verb; read literally it is a breeze rising.

clue.text: How a criminal is caught at the scene when the stage is set

definitions.text: How a criminal is caught at the scene when the stage is set

parts.words: How a criminal is caught at the scene when the stage is set
parts.note: a thief caught red-handed is caught during the deed; on stage, a play is divided into scenes and acts

explanation.surface: A crook is nabbed on the spot, in a theatrical setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre words 'scene' and 'stage' point to a play's division, while the crime reading means caught red-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught red-handed means caught while committing the deed, and a play's scene sits within an act.

clue.text: Benedictine in France is in charge of the house

parts.note: Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A French monk runs the household.
explanation.walkthrough: DOM is the honorific of Benedictine monks, as in Dom Perignon.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic describes things belonging to home and household life.

clue.text: Prince tells what happens to princes of the church

parts.note: relates means narrates or recounts

explanation.surface: A prince narrates the fates of royal heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops and archbishops are senior clergy, figuratively the princes of the church.

clue.text: It tells of one born in the settlement of Bethel

definitions.text: It tells of one born in the settlement of Bethel

indicators.note: a settlement is something settled or arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
b is the abbreviation for born in genealogies

explanation.surface: Scripture describes someone born in the biblical town of Bethel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement of' rearranges I, B and BETHEL; the whole clue also describes scripture, which tells of births in Bethel's region.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is the book which tells of Christ's birth and of the patriarchs at Bethel.

clue.text: An eyesore about Im back forms an obstacle

indicators.note: the eyelid swelling wraps around the reversed letters

parts.note: a stye is a sore swelling on the eyelid

indicators.note: back means the letters of Im are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, the contraction I'm without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an ugly sight blocks their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IM into MI, and 'about' puts that inside STYE. 'Eyesore' is a pun: not an ugly sight but a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a stymie was a ball blocking the putting line, hence any hindrance.

clue.text: Managed to find time which suited nicely

definitions.meaning: squeezed an appointment into a busy schedule
matched well, sat comfortably in place

explanation.surface: Someone squeezed in an appointment that worked out well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both scheduling something in and belonging comfortably.

clue.text: Japanese entertainer misrepresented his age

indicators.note: something misrepresented is distorted, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A performer from Japan lied about how old she was.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a woman trained to host and entertain with music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: Ultimately a teetotaller swallows gallons indiscriminately…

indicators.note: the abstainer's letters take in the rearranged letters

parts.note: TT is the abbreviation for a teetotaller, someone who drinks no alcohol

indicators.note: taken without order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: In the end, an abstainer gulps down huge quantities without care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indiscriminately' rearranges GALLONS to LONGLAS, and 'swallows' puts it inside TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally or in the end, after much delay or waiting.

clue.text: Delinquency roused city temper

indicators.note: stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Urban anger is stirred into lawbreaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor offences such as shoplifting or vandalism are what delinquency amounts to.

clue.text: … when working in a legal inn

definitions.text: when working in a legal inn

parts.words: when working in a legal inn
parts.note: a barrister practising law works in court; an inn also has a counter serving drinks

explanation.surface: Continuing the teetotaller's story: someone on the job at a lawyers' tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue's teetotaller. Barristers are called to the counsel's rail in court, and the Inns of Court are London's legal societies.
explanation.definitionFit: A practising barrister is said to be at the counsel's rail in court, and a pub's counter is also so named.

clue.text: Third degree in cooking

definitions.meaning: intense, harsh questioning of a suspect
heating food under direct heat

explanation.surface: A severe burn suffered in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh interrogation and cooking under a broiler share the same word.

clue.text: Queen'sorder to Anglicansis an order

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh

parts.note: taken as written with its s
CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A royal command to the Church of England is itself a command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges QUEENS and CE; the same word in the definition means a succession.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence is an ordered succession, one thing following another.

clue.text: Attended on being suddenly attacked

definitions.meaning: appeared or showed up on a date
rounded on someone without warning

explanation.surface: A guest who arrived on the day was set upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving on a day and rounding on someone are both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Cry-baby making a laughable mistake

definitions.meaning: one who wails loudly
a glaring blunder that provokes laughter

explanation.surface: A child's tantrum turns into an embarrassing error.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wails and a ludicrous blunder are both called by this word.

clue.text: Holiday worker accommodation available

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday
a worker ant is a common crossword worker

explanation.surface: Seasonal staff housing has a free room.
explanation.definitionFit: Unoccupied rooms or houses are free to be taken.

clue.text: Posted-one's pool entry it would seem

definitions.text: Posted-one's pool entry it would seem

parts.words: Posted-one's pool entry it would seem
parts.note: a bet placed in a pool is a stake, and posts driven into the ground are stakes too

explanation.surface: Someone sent off their football pools coupon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted' suggests mailing, but it means marked out with posts; the pools are a British football betting game.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked out with posts, or wagered as a bet, both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Arrest resulting from armed robbery

definitions.meaning: a halt or delay, stopping progress
a raid at gunpoint

explanation.surface: Police make a detention following a gunpoint raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A delay that stops progress and a robbery at gunpoint share the same word.

clue.text: No rating assigned for knowledge!

indicators.note: assigned suggests set out again, so these letters are redistributed

explanation.surface: A score of zero is given in a test of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assigned' rearranges NO RATING; the whole clue describes someone who scores nothing for learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or education earns no marks for it.

clue.text: Children one discovered in farm outhouses

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the farm buildings

parts.note: barns are farm buildings
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Kids were found hiding in the farm sheds.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRNS is the Scottish word for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish and northern English word for youngsters.

clue.text: Like a pointer pointing to a traffic jam

definitions.meaning: a pointer dog stands with its tail held stiffly out behind
a queue of vehicles backed up

explanation.surface: A signpost directs drivers to a congestion point.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog's rear held out behind, and a queue of vehicles stretching back, share the phrase.

clue.text: He makes a pile from the game

definitions.meaning: a maker of rugs, which have a pile
an informal British name for rugby union

explanation.surface: A man gets rich from sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' suggests a fortune, but it is the raised surface of a carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetiously a maker of floor mats, and British slang for rugby football.

clue.text: Italian and Egyptian severely criticised over and over again

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for said repeatedly

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian
to rate is an old word for to scold harshly

explanation.surface: An Italian and an Egyptian were scolded time and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated, said or done once more and then once more again.
